findings.description: POST /api/v1/urls is unauthenticated by spec (auth is a non-goal) and creates persistent rows and Redis counter consumption. Without throttling, the write path enables unbounded storage growth, alias squatting at scale, and mass creation of malicious short links.
findings.requirement: Implement rate limiting on POST /api/v1/urls (e.g., per-client-IP token bucket via a servlet filter or gateway-level control), returning 429 with application/problem+json. Limits must be configurable and documented in the README. If rate limiting is deferred to an upstream gateway, that decision must be explicitly recorded and the service must still enforce a conservative default limit.

findings.description: GET /{shortCode} issues a 302 to any stored long_url. The service is by design an open redirector; while destination scheme is restricted to http/https at write time, nothing prevents shortening links to phishing/malware destinations, and validation must not be bypassable (e.g., via 'javascript:', 'data:', userinfo tricks like https://trusted@evil.com, or whitespace/control characters in the URL).
findings.requirement: Validate long_url by parsing with java.net.URI: require an absolute URI, scheme exactly 'http' or 'https' (case-insensitive), a non-empty host, and reject URLs containing control characters, CR/LF, or embedded userinfo unless explicitly accepted. Persist and reflect the URL exactly as validated. The Location header must be set from the stored value without further interpolation. Note: blocklisting/reputation checking of destinations is not in the spec — if required it is a product decision, flagged as out of current scope, not silently assumed.

findings.description: Redirect responses echo attacker-supplied data (long_url) into the Location header. CRLF sequences surviving into the header enable HTTP response splitting / header injection.
findings.requirement: Reject any long_url containing CR, LF, or other ASCII control characters at validation time (400 problem+json), and rely on Spring's header-value sanitization as defense in depth. Add explicit unit tests for CRLF-injection payloads on both write (validation) and read (header emission) paths.

findings.description: The service requires Postgres and Redis credentials. The design does not state how secrets are supplied; hardcoding them in application.yml, the Dockerfile, or committed config would be a critical failure.
findings.requirement: All credentials (Postgres URL/user/password, Redis URI/password) must be supplied via environment variables or an external secret mechanism, never committed to the repository, baked into the Docker image, or present in the OpenAPI/README examples with real values. Testcontainers-generated credentials are exempt. Add a .gitignore/.dockerignore entry pattern for local env files and verify no secrets appear in logs at any level.

findings.description: long_url values frequently embed PII, session tokens, or capability URLs (e.g., signed links). The design mandates logging cache degradation and Redis fallback; if request/URL contents are logged verbatim, sensitive data leaks into logs. created_by is null in this scope, so no direct user PII is stored, but URLs themselves are sensitive.
findings.requirement: Log degradation events (Redis outage, cache bypass, counter fallback) with short_code and error class only — never the full long_url or request body at INFO/WARN. If long_url must appear in DEBUG logs, truncate and redact query strings. Ensure the global exception handler never includes stack traces, exception messages containing SQL/connection strings, or internal class names in problem+json 'detail' for 500 responses; log the correlation-worthy details server-side instead.

findings.description: Unhandled 500s route through the GlobalExceptionHandler. If the handler passes raw exception messages into ProblemDetail.detail, internal details (JDBC URLs, Redis hosts, Hibernate internals) leak to clients.
findings.requirement: For 500 responses, the problem+json body must contain a generic title/detail (e.g., 'Internal Server Error') and no exception message, stack trace, or internal identifiers. For 400 validation failures, detail may enumerate field-level violations but must not echo excessively long input values (truncate long_url echoes). Add an integration test asserting the 500 body shape.

findings.description: Custom aliases share the root path namespace with /api/v1 and any actuator/management endpoints. Although the ADR-12 regex prevents shadowing multi-segment paths, single-segment reserved words (e.g., 'api', 'actuator', 'health', 'admin') could still be registered as aliases, enabling confusing or deceptive links on the service's own domain.
findings.requirement: Maintain a configurable reserved-word blocklist for custom_alias (at minimum: 'api', 'actuator', 'health', 'admin', 'metrics', 'error') and reject matches with 400 problem+json. Confirm actuator endpoints (if enabled) are not exposed publicly on the same port without justification, or are restricted to liveness/readiness only.

findings.description: The write endpoint accepts JSON bodies; without size limits, oversized payloads or deeply nested JSON can exhaust resources. The 2048-char limit applies to long_url only, not the raw request.
findings.requirement: Enforce a maximum HTTP request body size for POST /api/v1/urls (e.g., server/Tomcat max post size and/or explicit content-length check, on the order of a few KB), rejecting oversized requests before deserialization. Configure short, explicit connection/command timeouts for Redis (already noted in RedisConfig) and Postgres so outages fail fast rather than exhausting threads.

findings.description: short_url is built from the configured app.base-url. If implementation instead derives it from the incoming Host header or X-Forwarded-* headers, attackers could poison generated short_urls (host header injection).
findings.requirement: Build short_url exclusively from the app.base-url configuration property (default http://localhost:8080), never from request headers. Document that production deployments must set app.base-url explicitly and should use https.

findings.description: Redis cache entries map short_code -> long_url. If Redis is shared or unauthenticated, a compromised or co-tenant client could poison cache entries, redirecting users to attacker destinations without touching Postgres.
findings.requirement: Document that Redis must be network-isolated and authenticated (requirepass/ACL) in production; use a key prefix/namespace (e.g., 'urlshort:cache:') to avoid collisions with other tenants. The design's cache-first read means poisoned entries are served without DB verification — this residual risk must be recorded in the README/threat notes since per-request verification would defeat the cache.

findings.description: Java 25 / Spring Boot 4 stack pulls Spring MVC, Spring Data JPA, Lettuce, Flyway, Testcontainers, and a Postgres driver. No dependency governance is stated in the design.
findings.requirement: Pin all dependency versions via the Spring Boot BOM plus explicit versions for anything outside it; add OWASP Dependency-Check or an equivalent SCA step to the build with a failure threshold for known critical CVEs; do not add dependencies beyond those needed for the stated deliverables without recording the addition. Base Docker image must be a minimal, digest-pinned JRE image running as a non-root user.

findings.description: Cache-Control: private is mandated (AC-7) which correctly prevents shared-cache storage of per-link redirects, but browsers may still cache 302s; a link later expiring (410) could continue redirecting from the browser cache.
findings.requirement: Emit Cache-Control: private as specified; additionally include 'no-store' or a bounded max-age only if the spec owner approves — this is an ambiguity to raise, not an assumption to make. At minimum, add 'no-store' consideration to the README's operational notes and ensure the 302 response contains no Set-Cookie or other sensitive headers.

findings.description: Sequential counter-based base62 codes are trivially enumerable, allowing bulk discovery of all shortened URLs (which may embed sensitive capability links). The spec mandates this scheme, so it cannot be changed unilaterally.
findings.requirement: Record enumeration as an accepted residual risk in the README/threat notes (spec-mandated design). Ensure rate limiting (SEC-1) also covers GET /{shortCode} lookups to slow scraping, and ensure 404 vs 410 responses do not include additional metadata beyond the problem+json basics.

required_controls: Input validation: strict Bean Validation plus programmatic java.net.URI parsing for long_url (absolute, http/https only, non-empty host, <=2048 chars, no control/CRLF characters, no userinfo); custom_alias ^[0-9a-zA-Z]{3,32}$ plus reserved-word blocklist; expiration_date must be well-formed ISO-8601 and strictly in the future; shortCode path variable regex-constrained at the mapping

Rate limiting: configurable per-client throttling on POST /api/v1/urls (and abuse-resistant limits on GET /{shortCode}), returning 429 problem+json; request body size cap enforced before deserialization

Secret handling: all datastore credentials via environment variables/externalized config; no secrets in source, Dockerfile, image layers, OpenAPI examples, or logs; Testcontainers credentials confined to test scope
PII: created_by remains null per spec; treat long_url as sensitive data — never log it in full, redact query strings, and do not include it in error responses beyond truncated validation echoes

Logging hygiene: degradation/fallback logs carry short_code and error class only; 500 problem+json bodies are generic with no stack traces, exception messages, or internal identifiers; no Set-Cookie or sensitive headers on redirects

Dependency policy: versions pinned via Spring Boot BOM, SCA/vulnerability scanning in the build with critical-CVE gating, minimal digest-pinned non-root base image in the Dockerfile, no unrecorded dependency additions

Infrastructure hygiene: Redis authenticated and network-isolated with namespaced keys, short command timeouts on Redis and Postgres clients, actuator exposure restricted to liveness/readiness, short_url built only from app.base-url configuration
high_impact_actions_expected: Create and apply Flyway database migrations (V1__create_urls_table.sql with CHECK constraints, V2__create_code_sequence.sql creating url_code_seq)

Add new third-party dependencies to the build (Spring Boot 4 starters, Spring Data JPA, Lettuce/Spring Data Redis, Flyway, Postgres driver, Testcontainers for Postgres and Redis, springdoc/OpenAPI tooling, optional rate-limiting library such as Bucket4j)
Create a Dockerfile (protected infrastructure artifact per layering rules — requires explicit approval since infra artifacts are declared out of agent scope)
Introduce a rate-limiting filter/configuration affecting all write-path traffic, including new 429 response semantics not currently in the OpenAPI document (OpenAPI update required)
Externalize and wire datastore secrets via environment-variable configuration in application profiles and the container entrypoint
Run Testcontainers-based integration tests that start ephemeral Postgres and Redis containers on the build host
Seed and mutate the global Redis counter (SETNX seed at 3844, batched INCRBY 1000) shared across all write instances
